summary: Training data for the last 4 weeks shows only a single open-water swim session (5.2km, 153 min), with no cycling, running, or strength sessions logged and almost entirely absent wellness data — this is a very low training load heading into a busy upcoming block. The nearest priority race is the Marathon in 99 days, targeting sub-4h (5:45/km), which requires consistent multi-disciplinary volume and progressive run build starting now. With the 10K race on 2026-11-08 also imminent, the focus should be on arriving at that race fresh while rebuilding aerobic base across all three disciplines.
suggestions: Prioritise consistency across all three disciplines immediately — with only one session logged in four weeks, the biggest risk to both the 10K on 8 Nov and the Marathon is detraining; stick rigidly to the upcoming plan as written for the next two weeks.

For the 10K race on 8 November, treat the Wk20 long ride on 7 Nov as a relaxed, easy-effort spin rather than a full 60km effort — arriving at race day with fresh legs matters more than completing the full ride distance.

Begin incorporating marathon-specific aerobic run volume from Wk21 onward — the 20km long runs in the plan are excellent base work, but ensure pace stays honest (6:15–6:45/km) rather than creeping faster, as aerobic conditioning is the limiting factor right now.

Track sleep and body battery consistently — nearly all wellness data is missing across the entire 4-week window, making it impossible to assess recovery quality; even manual logging will help calibrate training load decisions.

The swim pace in the open-water session (29:26/km ≈ ~2:57/100m) is above the pool target of ≤2:30/100m, so prioritise technique-focused pool sessions in Wk20 and Wk21 to close that gap ahead of the Ironman build later.
